clue.text: Helps her putt in tight game

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, so these letters are reeling about into a new order

explanation.surface: A golfer's partner helps her hole a putt in a close match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight game' looks like a close contest, but 'tight' (drunk) is the anagram signal. The answer is an old children's party game of passing a shoe secretly around a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional parlour game in which players pass a slipper secretly around a seated ring.

clue.text: Association to raise flag

parts.note: a union is an association of workers or states
to jack something up is to raise it

explanation.surface: A society decides to hoist a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: The Union Jack is the national flag of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Type of hacksaw found in kindergarten once

indicators.note: says the letters sit inside the run of words kindergarten once

explanation.surface: A kind of saw was once kept in a nursery school.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon saw is a small stiff-backed saw used for cutting joints, so the name labels a kind of saw.

clue.text: Had editor describing old article as rash

indicators.note: describing in its old sense of drawing a line around, so one group of letters encloses the other

parts.note: taken as written
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An editor wrote up an antique article as reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its old sense of drawing round, so the first pair of words wraps the second, opening after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hotheaded acts impetuously without thinking, which is being reckless.

clue.text: Man of high social standing also blowing top

indicators.note: losing one's top means the first letter is lost from the phrase meaning also

parts.note: as well means also

explanation.surface: A society gentleman also loses his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' reads as losing one's temper, but it removes the first letter of AS WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell is old-fashioned slang for a smartly dressed, fashionable gentleman.

clue.text: Night out? Not for me!

parts.note: a night out usually means an evening of fun, but here it is a night spent awake, which this sufferer cannot escape

explanation.definitionFit: A person with chronic sleeplessness lies awake through the night unable to drift off.

clue.text: Explorer needs a jacket for cold weather

parts.note: Mungo Park was a Scottish explorer of the Niger

explanation.surface: An explorer requires a warm coat for the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof coat designed for very cold conditions.

clue.text: Bureaucracy reduced gradually once parts exchanged

indicators.note: the two sections of the word swap places, the tail coming to the front

parts.note: something tapered narrows little by little

explanation.surface: Officialdom was slowly cut back after departments were swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: TAPERED splits as TAPE and RED; exchanging the parts gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Red tape is excessive official procedure, the classic complaint about bureaucracy.

clue.text: Sketches large number in outskirts of Dungeness

indicators.note: the large number goes inside the outer letters of the place name
the outskirts are the first and last letters of the word Dungeness

parts.note: a raft of things is a large number of them

explanation.surface: An artist makes drawings of many things on the edge of Dungeness, a shingle headland in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Drafts are preliminary versions or rough drawings of a design.

clue.text: Rule, then abdicate not having son

indicators.note: the word for abdicate is shown without the letter for son

parts.note: to abdicate is to resign a throne or office
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A monarch rules, then gives up the throne for lack of an heir.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is the period of a sovereign's rule, and to reign is to rule.

clue.text: Valuable step certain to be taken on board

indicators.note: one word is carried inside another, as cargo on a ship

parts.note: a tread is a step on a stair or a footstep
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A sure step aboard a ship is a valuable one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasured is held dear and highly prized.

clue.text: Intended to keep name back

indicators.note: one word holds the other within it

parts.note: your intended is your fiance

explanation.surface: Someone means to keep a name in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like part of 'keep name back' but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To finance a venture is to fund or support it with money.

clue.text: Greek character holding a dance

indicators.note: the Greek letter wraps around the single letter

parts.note: lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek figure leads a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast Brazilian partner dance popular in the late 1980s.

clue.text: Move across a step

indicators.note: the word for move lies across the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to stir is to move slightly

explanation.surface: Someone shifts sideways along a step.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is a single step in a flight.

clue.text: Check made by coach during intermission

indicators.note: the coach sits within the intermission

parts.note: a rest is a break or pause
to train is to coach

explanation.surface: A coach makes a check during a half-time break.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is a check or curb on action.

clue.text: Playing field's ending marriage

indicators.note: the last letter of the word field's is taken

parts.note: an alliance is a union such as a marriage

explanation.surface: A footballer's time on the pitch ends his marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalliance is idle trifling or amorous toying, a kind of playing about.

clue.text: Desperate, the French duke in pain

parts.note: la is a French word for the

indicators.note: the duke goes inside the word for pain

parts.note: a stitch is a sharp pain in the side

explanation.surface: A French duke is in desperate pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a final desperate attempt to avoid defeat.

clue.text: Name suprisingly moderate building by the Seine

indicators.note: a surprise rearranges expectations, so the letters of moderate are rearranged

explanation.surface: A guidebook names a moderate building beside the Paris river.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is printed misspelt as 'suprisingly'; it rearranges MODERATE to OTREDAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame cathedral stands on the Ile de la Cite in the Seine in Paris.

clue.text: Support one group over another study by banks

parts.note: to take a subject is to study it
the banks of a river are its sides

explanation.surface: Someone studies beside a river and backs one faction.
explanation.definitionFit: To take sides is to align with one party in a dispute.

clue.text: Handler's shoe

definitions.meaning: one who trains and handles animals or athletes
a sports shoe, especially for running

explanation.definitionFit: Trainer means both a coach of people or animals and a soft sports shoe.

clue.text: Hear start of carol at church

indicators.note: the first letter of carol is taken

explanation.surface: Listen for the opening carol at church.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a remark is to hear or make it out.

clue.text: I'd study after hours, out of sight

indicators.note: after places the pieces for I'd and study behind the letter for hours

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: Someone studies late into the night, tucked away.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden means concealed, kept away from view.

clue.text: One failing to gain a place in a lyceum, initially so put out

definitions.text: One failing to gain a place

indicators.note: the first letters of a and lyceum are taken

parts.note: taken as written
a paper that ran a story put it out

explanation.surface: A student at a school, put out, fails to get into the top places.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a horse or competitor finishing outside the placings, so a loser.

clue.text: Attack head of sixth-form college

indicators.note: the first letter of sixth-form is taken

parts.note: Eton College is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: The head of a sixth-form college comes under attack.
explanation.definitionFit: To set on someone is to assault or attack them.

clue.text: Relative, English, in Riviera resort

indicators.note: the letter for English goes inside the resort

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: An English relative stays in a Riviera resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is the daughter of one's brother or sister.

clue.text: Boring side is going nowhere

parts.note: dead means dull or boring
an end is a side in sport, as in changing ends

explanation.surface: A dull team is getting nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead-end job or route leads nowhere and offers no progress.

clue.text: Almost done in, lying under a tree

indicators.note: in a down entry the shortened word sits below the letter a
the word for done in loses its last letter

parts.note: spent means exhausted, done in

explanation.surface: Exhausted, someone lies beneath a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar tree known for its trembling leaves.

clue.text: Food freak — term, I fancy, used around noon

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or freak, as in a health nut

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the letter for noon
fancy as in fanciful, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A health freak tells you the term for food at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges the letters of 'term I' to RIMET, which goes around N to make RIMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutriment is nourishment, the substance in food that sustains life.

clue.text: Spot soft fabric

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft
lace is a delicate openwork fabric

explanation.surface: A spot on soft fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a location or position, as in a nice spot for a picnic.

clue.text: Employ alternative methods, as campanologists do?

definitions.meaning: to vary one's approach by trying different ways
bell-ringers sound sets of bells in varying sequences

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes bell-ringing sequences and figuratively means varying one's approach.
